summary: Virtual Smart Card initialization fails post SCCM driver hash rotation on depot-repaired workstations
description: Issue summary: After a depot repair where SCCM applied the latest driver bundle (hash rotation deployed 2026-02-17), affected Windows 11 machines intermittently fail to initialize the Virtual Smart Card (VSC) subsystem during first boot post-reprovision. Impact: Users are unable to complete local credential enrollment and SSO flows that rely on VSC-backed keys. This blocks a small number of devs and platform engineers receiving repaired hardware. Environment: Corporate depot images (image-2026-02), machines rebuilt via SCCM task sequence, region: us-east, image applied on repaired hardware. Steps to reproduce: 1) Depot repair -> wipe and SCCM image (image-2026-02) 2) During OOBE, complete local provisioning steps 3) Run onboarding script that triggers VSC initialization 4) Observe failure in credential enrollment Expected behavior: VSC service starts, keys are provisioned, and Windows Hello / SSO enrollment completes. Actual behavior: VSC init fails with device-service errors and the onboarding script times out after 10 minutes. Workaround: Manual driver rollback (see resolution) or skip VSC provisioning and use temporary password until a repaired image is applied.
steps_to_reproduce:
1. Build or take a repaired machine and apply SCCM task sequence image-2026-02.
2. Boot to OOBE and complete account creation.
3. Run corp-onboard.ps1 (included in image) or allow auto-run onboarding.
4. Observe onboarding log at C:\ProgramData\CorpOnboard\onboard.log; VSC steps fail between 'vsc-init' and 'vsc-provision' with timeouts.
logs:
Error snippet from C:\ProgramData\CorpOnboard\onboard.log:
[2026-02-18T09:12:02Z] vsc-init: starting
[2026-02-18T09:12:05Z] vsc-init: failed to load driver package (0x000000E9)
[2026-02-18T09:12:05Z] vsc-init: service start timeout (Error 0x800705B4)
Windows Event ID 7026: 'The following boot-start or system-start driver(s) failed to load: VSCFilter'
SCCM log (smsts.log): 'Driver package hash mismatch - applied package hash 3f7a... expected 4b2c... - skipping signature enforcement check disabled: false'
investigation_notes: 2026-02-18 10:00 - Intake: Depot tech reported 5/23 repaired machines failed VSC enrollment post image apply.
Verified correlation with SCCM driver bundle rotation deployed 2026-02-17 (package id pkg-drivers-2026-02).
Reproduced failure on 2 lab devices (Dell 7440, Lenovo X1) with image-2026-02 task sequence.

Observed smsts reports where driver package hash in manifest does not match local unpacked driver hash on some repaired HW serials -> smsts skipped driver installation causing VSC kernel driver missing.

Hypothesis: SCCM package rotation changed signing metadata; for previously repaired hardware with non-standard NIC/ECU, unpack ordering produced hash mismatch under our cache validation, causing SCCM to skip critical VSC driver (VSCFilter.sys).
Checked driver catalog signing: signatures valid, but SCCM content library record uses pre-rotation hash; cache-renew path can cause stale blobs on depot server nodes.
Temporary reproduction using forcing re-download (ccmsetup /downloadcontent) re-applied drivers and allowed VSC to initialize.
Escalated to Imaging/Provisioning infra (PR #7b3f2c1) to add cache-bust and stronger validation; opened linked infra PR for package rotation checklist.
Risk assessment: moderate. Affects small batch of depot-repaired machines until full cache refresh rolled; potential to block onboarding for returning devices.

Next steps: rollback driver rotation on affected depot pool, trigger content library update on depot SCCM nodes, add validation step to task sequence to verify VSCFilter.sys presence before completing onboarding.
Related runbook page reviewed and flagged for update to include 'verify VSC driver present' check in 2.0 task sequence.

resolution: Partial rollback applied to affected depot nodes (pkg-drivers-2026-01); content library refresh forced across depot cluster. Manual driver reinstallation steps added to follow-up INT-333215 for remaining machines. Imaging task sequence will be updated to validate presence of VSCFilter.sys and to force content re-download on mismatch. Long-term: add package-rotation checklist and automated cache-bust in SCCM orchestration PR (see related_github_prs).
